sentences.text: They are in custody since 19th July, 2024 and 4th March, 2024, respectively.

It is alleged in the FIR that the appellants committed offence(s) punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471,
477, 477-A, 408, 409, 201, 216, 109 read with Sections 34, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860,
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Rajasthan Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1992,
and Section 66-D of the Information and Technology Act, 2000.
4.

entities.text: Rajasthan Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1992
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5. The prosecution proposes to examine around 150 witnesses to drive home the charges against the appellant and the co-accused, being 133 in number.
Of them 57 accused have been granted bail.
6. Having regard to the fact and circumstances, there is every likelihood of the trial taking sufficient time to conclude.

Since number of co-accused have been granted bail, we are inclined to accept the present appeals.
7.

Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment(s) and order(s).
8.
The appellants shall be released on bail, subject to such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the trial court.
9. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.

10. The appellants shall, however, appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless exempted;
and should the appellants fail to appear on any date without justifiable cause or breach any of the terms and conditions for grant of bail, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail.
11. The appeals are, accordingly, allowed on the aforesaid terms.
12. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.

.............................J. [DIPANKAR DATTA] ..............................J. [AUGUSTINE GEORGE MASIH] New Delhi;
December 05, 2025.
